title: Qworld: Question-Specific Evaluation Criteria for LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2603.23522v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) on open-ended questions is difficult because response quality depends on the question's context. Binary scores and static rubrics fail to capture these context-dependent requirements. Existing methods define criteria at the dataset level or generate them in a single pass, which limits their ability to explore the evaluation space implied by each question. We introduce One-Question-One-World (Qworld), a method that generates question-specific evaluation criteria using a recursive expansion tree. Given a question, Qworld decomposes it into scenarios, perspectives, and fine-grained binary criteria through hierarchical and horizontal expansion. The resulting criteria specify what a high-quality answer must address for that question. translated_title: Qworld：针对大语言模型的特定问题评估标准
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2603.23522v2 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：评估大型语言模型（LLMs）在开放式问题上的表现是困难的，因为回答质量取决于问题的上下文。二元评分和静态评分标准无法捕捉这些依赖于上下文的要求。现有方法在数据集层面定义标准或一次性生成标准，这限制了它们探索每个问题所隐含的评估空间的能力。我们引入了“一个问题一个世界”（Qworld），一种使用递归扩展树生成特定问题评估标准的方法。给定一个问题，Qworld通过层次和水平扩展将其分解为场景、视角和细粒度的二元标准。生成的标准明确了一个高质量回答必须涵盖的内容。在HealthBench上，Qworld覆盖了89%的专家撰写的标准，并生成了79%经人类专家验证的新颖标准。专家们对Qworld标准的评分高于现有方法。
tldr: Qworld通过递归扩展树生成特定于问题的评估标准，显著提升了开放性问题评估的覆盖率和新颖性，并获得了专家认可。
en_tdlr: Qworld generates question-specific evaluation criteria via a recursive expansion tree, significantly improving coverage and novelty for open-ended question assessment, with expert validation.
